To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a smart speaker driver is developed that can deliver 1 W at 1 % THD into a low impedance load, that can be operated from a 1.5 V battery and that is protected against speaker damage.
we have designed a smart speaker driver with an integrated DC-DC boost and a current sensing ADC.

we have designed a class-D smart amplifier that can deliver 3.2 W of audio power into an 8 Ω load at a 5% THD and that can estimate the speaker membrane excursion and voice-coil temperature to protect the speaker from over-excursion and overheating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and evaluation of the first class-D speaker driver that combines a high output power, a high efficiency, an accurate speaker protection algorithm and a small chip area.
the design of a smart speaker driver that can deliver high output power and is robust against speaker damage.
the design and implementation of an adaptive speaker driver that can be used in smart speakers and wireless audio systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design has the potential to be a good choice for the implementation of a smart class-D speaker driver.
the proposed system is a very good solution for the application of a smart speaker driver.
this work is a very nice example of how to combine several techniques to obtain a very high performance audio amplifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed system is the first smart speaker driver that is fully integrated in CMOS and is able to drive a loudspeaker with a high power level while maintaining high efficiency at low supply voltage.
we have successfully implemented a smart speaker driver with adaptive speaker protection on a single chip.
the presented class-D smart speaker system has a very high efficiency, a very low power dissipation, an adaptive speaker protection, a low-cost implementation and a very small form factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design a smart speaker driver that is small enough and low power to fit into a portable device.
the speaker current can be accurately measured by sampling the current at the moments where its average value is equal to the instantaneous current.
the proposed system is able to deliver high power and protect the speaker at the same time, while the chip area is kept small.
